rows.body: Confirm with Alpha Brand Studios / Choice for Blu standards manual vintage and agreement year

Upper-upscale brands under the Choice portfolio share central reservations, loyalty, and reporting while maintaining distinct Nordic Nouveau guestroom and public-space standards. Owners should treat requirements as agreement- and prototype-specific: design-forward public spaces, signature F&B, and gallery-curator service rituals typically exceed core Radisson conversion scope—budget for upper-upscale FF&E, baths, and QA from LOI.

rows.title: Brand Identity & Guest Experience
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Think in Black & White Blu arrival, Nordic Nouveau corridors, and Enticing Moments rituals—scent, music, and gallery-curator touchpoints are usually prescribed.
Owner planning consideration: Map mandatory opening items vs phased Curatorial Warmth elements; budget approved vendors for upper-upscale casegoods.
Typical status: Confirm with Alpha Brand Studios
Notes to confirm: Applies to new build, conversion, and reflag. Sister-flag from core Radisson may reuse limited FF&E only with written waivers.

rows.title: Guestroom, Bath & Sleep Experience
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Nordic Nouveau modules, lighting scenes, and bath packages tie to approved prototypes—linen and mattress programs are usually mandated.
Owner planning consideration: Casegoods lead times drive CALA opening dates; room-type PIP schedules common on conversion.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to all guest-facing projects. Non-visible deferrals only with written brand approval.

rows.title: Public Space, Lobby & upper-upscale positioning
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Lobby zoning, meeting pre-function, and social spaces may need to reflect upper-upscale positioning—furniture families, art, and digital guest messaging are commonly controlled.
Owner planning consideration: Ceiling heights, storefront, and co-tenancy rules affect entitlement; upper-upscale refresh can exceed select-service conversion cost.
Applies to: New build and conversion
Typical status: Confirm with brand

rows.title: Food, Beverage & Social Spaces
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Signature restaurant, bar, or marketplace concepts are prototype-driven—kitchen, hood, and liquor scope vary by CALA market.
Owner planning consideration: Model self-op vs lease and gallery-curator staffing before LOI; F&B audits protect Enticing Moments delivery.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to properties with in-scope F&B. Contract operators still need Blu concept approval.

rows.title: Meetings, Events & Group Business
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Meeting room counts, divisible walls, AV standards, and group sales tooling may be specified for upper-upscale urban and suburban prototypes.
Owner planning consideration: Load-in, ballroom stack, and telecom backbone affect core-and-shell; group mix assumptions tie to brand sales support.
Applies to: Hotels with meeting inventory
Typical status: Confirm with brand

rows.title: Technology, CRS & Loyalty Programs
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Choice CRS/PMS, Wi-Fi, digital key, and mobile journeys for Inspired Professional guests—Choice Privileges cutover is usually mandatory.
Owner planning consideration: Parallel runs and channel-manager mapping to protect rate parity during conversion.
Typical status: Contractual cutover in agreement
Notes to confirm: Applies to all operating hotels. Limited legacy transition only with brand approval.

rows.title: Design Review, Plans & Submittals
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Design-forward prototype and public-space narrative submittals gate construction—Nordic Nouveau guestroom modules are milestone-critical.
Owner planning consideration: Budget Alpha Brand Studios review fees, interior rework, and float for upper-upscale resubmittals.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to new build and material renovation. Recent upper-upscale sister work may qualify for abbreviated review—document in writing.

rows.title: PIP, Conversion & Sister-Flag Transitions
rows.body:
Typical consideration: PIP itemizes Nordic Nouveau casegoods, public-space narrative, signage, and tech—core Radisson sister conversions rarely skip upper-upscale scope.
Owner planning consideration: Tie PIP to key money; separate opening-mandatory vs 12–24 month deferrals in LOI.
Typical status: Often negotiated
Notes to confirm: Applies to conversion and reflag. Recent upper-upscale PIP within 24–36 months may reduce scope—confirm in writing.

rows.title: QA, Inspection & Ongoing Compliance
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Pre-opening and annual QA score Nordic Nouveau rooms, F&B theater, and Curatorial Warmth service—not generic upscale checklists.
Owner planning consideration: Reserve capital for public-space and casegoods remediation; repeat failures can trigger reinspection fees.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to opening and stabilized operations.

rows.title: Sustainability, Accessibility & Life Safety
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Upper-upscale sustainability and accessibility targets may exceed code; life safety reviews are non-negotiable for Inspired Professional confidence.
Owner planning consideration: Coordinate EV, water, and accessible room dispersion during Nordic Nouveau design—not as a late add-on.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to new build and renovation.

When moving within the Choice family, owners often sequence loyalty cutover, CRS/PMS migration, signage, and soft-goods refresh before a full public-space rebuild. Confirm whether Radisson upper-upscale positioning under Alpha Brand Studios adds mandatory design elements beyond the prior flag, and whether any items from a recent sister-brand PIP can carry forward with waivers.
